title: How ‘Final Fantasy VII Revelation’ Strikes the Balance Between Old and New
gist: Square Enix studio head and director Naoki Hamaguchi previews Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the final part of the decade-long Remake trilogy. He describes a planet-scale open world, greatly expanded areas like Wutai, an excess of content that had to be held back, and a deliberate push to recast Final Fantasy as a gameplay-first franchise that can compete with celebrated open-world titles.

themes.theme: Too much content, not too little

insights.claim: Hamaguchi says that after two 100-plus-hour games, Revelation's problem was too much content, not too little. The team had to be careful about what it included, which contradicts online speculation that the third part would be padded.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: A content-heavy final installment points to a long-tail engagement play for a major Square Enix title.
insights.quote: I was sat there like, ‘No, this is the opposite problem!’

insights.claim: In response to complaints about Rebirth's size, Revelation adds a chapter select for repeat playthroughs and tones down Rebirth's notoriously difficult, repetitive trophy requirements. Hamaguchi says variety matters more than volume.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: Square Enix is adjusting to player feedback, which could broaden the game's audience.
insights.locator: There are a few olive branches

insights.claim: Hamaguchi claims Revelation may be the only game with a truly 'planetary-scale' open world. Players can fly Cid's airship, the Highwind, and parachute down to explore.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: This is how the game is positioned against other open-world AAA releases.
insights.locator: Along with the sizable new areas

insights.claim: Wutai, two huts on the world map in the 1997 original, has become a vast, thriving city that players explore on Chocobos, an example of the trilogy's expanded and reordered structure.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: The expanded scope means high production investment in the trilogy finale.
insights.locator: One of the biggest examples is the nation of Wutai

insights.claim: Hamaguchi says his main goal is to change how people see Final Fantasy, from story-focused to gameplay-led, so that it can stand alongside acclaimed open-world titles and bring in more fans.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: This is a franchise-expansion strategy aimed at players outside the core JRPG audience.
insights.quote: I also wanted to really showcase the gameplay
insights.locator: “I think that a lot of people have the image

insights.claim: Hamaguchi says the trilogy's story is 'multilayered' rather than a multiverse, and that the word the team uses most is 'reunion'. He notes they began on these themes more than seven years ago, before multiverse stories saturated media.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: This narrative framing tries to distance the game from 'multiverse fatigue'.
insights.quote: Actually, the word that comes up most often is ‘reunion.’

insights.claim: Hamaguchi says people are now entering the games industry because Final Fantasy VII Remake inspired them, which he sees as the trilogy building the franchise's future talent pipeline.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: The trilogy has long-term value to Square Enix's brand and its ability to attract talent.
